title: Formal diagram categories and normalized restriction models
statement: Let $p:\mathcal F\to\mathcal B$ be a functor between categories, $D:I\to\mathcal B$ a diagram, $T\in\mathcal B$, and $\iota:D\to\operatorname{const}_I T$ a natural transformation. Categories fibred in groupoids use the convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], with universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Define $\operatorname{FormalDiagram}(p,D)$ to be the fibre over $D$ of postcomposition $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal F)\to\operatorname{Fun}(I,\mathcal B)$. Objects are lifts $s:I\to\mathcal F$ with $ps=D$, and arrows are natural transformations over the identity of $D$. A normalized restriction model consists of a functor $R:\mathcal F_T\to\operatorname{FormalDiagram}(p,D)$, arrows $r_{x,i}:R(x)_i\to x$ strongly cartesian over $\iota_i$, with $R(x)(h)r_{x,j}=r_{x,i}$ for every $h:i\to j$, and $R(a)_i r_{y,i}=r_{x,i}a$ for every vertical arrow $a:x\to y$. Here $\mathcal F_T$ is the fibre category. For a category fibred in groupoids and the positive adic diagram, these are the compatible formal systems and the cartesian characterization of their restriction functor; all automorphisms are retained.
